memory_update.text: PANW should be kept as the reference benchmark for this node after closing CyberArk and Chronosphere; it is not underfollowed but defines how the market prices integrated identity/security/observability platforms.

FROG enters the underfollowed lane as a software supply-chain security and artifact governance candidate tied to AI/cloud development complexity; verify security revenue mix and retention before promotion.
PD enters the underfollowed lane as a small-cap operations automation/AIOps candidate; thesis depends on whether AI-agent and automation features revive expansion metrics.
TENB enters the underfollowed lane as cloud/AI exposure-management software; verify Tenable One and cloud-security contribution versus crowded CNAPP and vulnerability-management competition.

HashiCorp and Informatica were strong node fits historically, but HashiCorp was acquired by IBM and Informatica was acquired by Salesforce, so they should be treated as embedded exposure through IBM/CRM rather than standalone US-listed candidates in this layer.

node: Cloud security, machine identity, observability, infrastructure automation, data governance, and workload orchestration software
summary: Layer 1B expansion found one reference consolidator and three smaller direct-exposure software names. The strongest direct public reference is Palo Alto Networks because it has absorbed CyberArk for identity/machine identity and Chronosphere for cloud-native observability. The underfollowed lane contains JFrog for software supply-chain security and secrets exposure, PagerDuty for operations-cloud automation and incident response, and Tenable for cloud/AI security posture and exposure management. These are research candidates only, not recommendations; later layers should test revenue purity, retention, free cash flow quality, competitive displacement risk, and whether AI/cloud complexity is actually translating into durable incremental demand.
